extracted.intended_audience: public health authorities, outbreak response communication teams, WHO country/regional communicators
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and implementing a public-health outbreak communication plan: defines principles, plan components, roles, messaging, media relations, community engagement, rumor management, monitoring and evaluation for communicating about infectious disease outbreaks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core principles of outbreak communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Sets out fundamental guiding principles for outbreak communication such as building and maintaining trust, announcing early, being transparent, listening to public concerns, and planning ahead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply these principles consistently in all communications. 'Announce early' means provide initial information promptly even when details are incomplete; 'be transparent' requires stating what is known and unknown; 'build trust' demands honesty and timely follow-up. Use the principles to evaluate every public message and action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparedness: written outbreak communication plan
rubrics_metrics.description: A formal, pre-existing communication plan that documents objectives, target audiences, key messages, channels, roles and responsibilities, resources, approval workflows and contingencies for likely outbreak scenarios.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The plan should be practical and actionable (templates, contact lists, pre-approved messages). Include trigger criteria for activating the plan, checklists for rapid press releases, and plans for surge capacity and 24/7 communications. Regularly update and test the plan through exercises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leadership, roles and coordination
rubrics_metrics.description: Clear designation of lead communication authority, incident spokesperson(s), and a coordination mechanism across health sector partners and other relevant agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define who authorizes public statements, who is the media contact, and how agencies will harmonize messaging. Maintain a roster of trained spokespersons and an incident communications team with defined shifts, handover procedures and escalation paths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience identification and segmentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Systematic identification and analysis of target audiences (general public, affected communities, health workers, vulnerable groups, media, partners) and tailoring of messages to their information needs and cultural/linguistic contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Map audiences by risk level, channels they use, languages, literacy and trust networks. Prioritize reach to high-risk and hard-to-reach groups and adapt format (audio/visual/print) accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Message development: clarity and actionability
rubrics_metrics.description: Messages must be clear, concise, factual, non-technical and provide specific protective actions for the audience. Messages should state the situation, risks, recommended actions and where to get help or more information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use plain language, avoid jargon, be specific about behaviours to adopt, and include calls-to-action. Test messages with audience representatives and pre-position core messages for rapid adaptation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness and speed of communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide information quickly and regularly; update the public as new information becomes available. Early announcements are preferred over waiting for full certainty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish timelines for initial public notification and scheduled updates. Even brief initial statements are valuable; follow-up with more detail as facts are confirmed. Monitor and shorten approval chains to avoid delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and honesty about uncertainty
rubrics_metrics.description: Be open about what is known, what is unknown, and what is being done to learn more. Avoid false reassurance; explain uncertainties plainly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When facts are incomplete, state that investigations are underway, explain expected timelines, and commit to follow-up communications. Transparency builds credibility and reduces speculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-way communication and listening
rubrics_metrics.description: Mechanisms to listen to community concerns, questions and rumours and to adapt communications and response based on feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish hotlines, community meetings, social-listening systems, and feedback loops with community leaders. Use monitoring results to refine messages and address misconceptions directly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media relations and press releases
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for preparing and issuing press releases and conducting media briefings including required content (what happened, where, who is affected, guidance, contact information), structure, timing and spokesperson practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Press releases should include a clear headline, situation summary, current advice, resources/contacts, and quotes from the authorized spokesperson. Provide backgrounders and FAQs. Coordinate timing across agencies to ensure consistent information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rumour, misinformation and hoax management
rubrics_metrics.description: Active monitoring for rumours and misinformation and procedures to rapidly assess, correct and prevent harmful misinformation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use media monitoring and social listening to detect circulating falsehoods. Respond quickly with factual corrections using trusted messengers and appropriate channels. Prioritize rumours that could change public behaviour or undermine response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Channel selection and use of media platforms
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose and use the mix of communication channels appropriate to each audience: traditional media, social media, community networks, SMS, hotlines, posters and local radio/TV.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match channel to audience reach and trust; maintain official web/social accounts for rapid updates; ensure simultaneous release across platforms where appropriate and adapt content format to channel norms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spokesperson selection and media training
rubrics_metrics.description: Appoint credible, trained spokespeople who can deliver consistent messages and manage interviews, and ensure they receive regular media and risk-communication training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spokespeople should be recognizable, prepared to explain uncertainty, and briefed before media appearances. Use message maps and Q&A to prepare; avoid conflicting statements by uncoordinated actors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk communication aimed at behaviour change
rubrics_metrics.description: Design communication to enable and motivate protective behaviours: explain risk clearly, provide feasible protective steps, address barriers and use positive, practical messaging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply behavioural insights: make actions simple, actionable and socially supported; provide rationale for measures; use credible role models and community influencers to promote uptake.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community engagement and social mobilization
rubrics_metrics.description: Actively involve communities, civil society, religious and traditional leaders in planning and delivering messages and interventions to ensure acceptability and uptake.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Co-develop messages with community representatives, use community-based channels for dissemination, and involve local actors in two-way dialogue and monitoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring and evaluation of communication activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Define indicators and methods to monitor outputs (e.g., press releases issued), reach (media coverage, social-media metrics), outcomes (knowledge, attitudes, behaviours) and use findings to adapt strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish baseline measures, track media and social metrics, conduct rapid knowledge/behaviour surveys, document lessons and conduct after-action reviews to improve future responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phased communication and escalation triggers
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe communication approaches by outbreak phase (preparedness, detection, escalation, recovery) and define triggers for message escalation or changes in tone and content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Map messages, channels and responsible actors to each phase. Define thresholds (case numbers, geographic spread) that require activating specific communications or higher-level coordination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical and equity considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure communications respect privacy, avoid stigmatization, and address the needs of vulnerable or marginalized populations with equitable access to information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid naming or blaming affected groups, provide accessible formats and translations, and ensure messaging does not discriminate. Protect personally identifiable information in public communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation, approvals and record-keeping
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain records of all public communications (press releases, media briefings, social posts), approvals given, and rationale for messaging decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep a communications log with timestamps, sender/approver, distribution lists and links to materials to enable accountability and after-action review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capacity building, training and simulation exercises
rubrics_metrics.description: Regular training of communications staff and exercises to rehearse message development, media briefings, rumor control and coordination under emergency conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Schedule tabletop and field exercises, evaluate performance, update SOPs and provide refresher trainings on media handling and risk communication principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partnerships and harmonized messaging across agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Mechanisms to coordinate messaging with partners (local authorities, NGOs, international agencies) to avoid contradictory information and maximize reach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create joint communication lines, shared message repositories and regular coordination meetings to harmonize public statements and response advice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logistics and resourcing for communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure budget, staffing, technical infrastructure, printing and media-buys are allocated to support sustained communications during an outbreak.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan for surge staffing, media monitoring tools, translation services and materials production. Include contracting/agreements with media and vendors in preparedness plans.
